epics.title: SHA-256 Document Deduplication, Re-Upload Interception & Legacy Duplicate Merge
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator or admission officer uploads PDF or DOCX documents to the CRIE portal, I want uploaded files fingerprinted with SHA-256 and checked against stored documents before creating rows, so that duplicate document entries are prevented, previously extracted structured records can be reviewed or updated immediately, and legacy duplicates (IDs 1, 10, and 11) are merged without losing linked records.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% duplicate document rows created on identical re-uploads and 100% foreign-key relationship retention after merging legacy IDs 1, 10, and 11
epics.tocConstraintRef: Absence of content_sha256 fingerprinting and pre-insert lookup in the document ingestion pipeline causing redundant document rows and split extracted records
requirements: R1: Compute and persist content_sha256 (with secondary matching by normalized filename and extracted text byte length) in the SQLite documents table and crie_document_engine.py.

R2: Intercept matching file re-uploads in crie_assistant_api.py without inserting a duplicate document row, returning deduplicated=true, the original document ID, the list of already extracted structured DB records, and a prompt offering to update or correct those records.

R3: Provide an idempotent SQLite migration and cleanup script in scripts/ that consolidates existing duplicate documents (IDs 1, 10, and 11) into a single canonical ID while re-pointing all linked structured-table and session references without data loss, supporting dry-run and backup verification.
R4: Handle corrupted, unreadable, or failed hash/DB operations atomically with explicit error feedback and zero orphan rows while preserving the user's selected upload context.

R5: Render upload deduplication feedback in the browser UI showing the deduplicated status, original document ID, extracted-record summary, and accessible actions to inspect or update records, compliant with mobile layouts and WCAG 2.1 AA.

R6: Include realistic CRIE sample document fixtures (such as residency and postgraduate admission order PDFs) and verify hash deduplication, API re-upload responses, and legacy ID 1/10/11 merge integrity across unit, integration, and E2E tests.

slices.title: Schema content_sha256 Column & Engine Hashing
slices.jtbd: When implementing document fingerprinting for this epic, I want content_sha256 calculation, normalized filename plus text-length fallback matching, and schema indexing in crie_document_engine.py, so that duplicate content is reliably detected before SQLite insertion.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an uploaded PDF or DOCX byte stream, When crie_document_engine.py computes the fingerprint, Then a lowercase hex content_sha256 digest and normalized filename/text-size key are produced deterministically and persisted in the SQLite documents table.
Given an existing document row matching by content_sha256 or normalized filename and text byte length, When the deduplication lookup executes, Then it returns the canonical document record without inserting a new row.
Given an unreadable file or database constraint error during hashing, When the transaction fails, Then changes roll back cleanly with an explicit error and zero orphan rows in SQLite.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Missing indexed content_sha256 column and deterministic text normalization in crie_document_engine.py
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% deterministic SHA-256 digest generation and <5ms indexed lookup latency on 1,000+ stored documents

slices.title: Legacy Duplicate Documents Merge Migration (IDs 1, 10, 11)
slices.jtbd: When implementing legacy data consolidation for this epic, I want an idempotent migration script in scripts/merge_duplicate_documents.py that merges document IDs 1, 10, and 11, so that all existing structured-table links are preserved under one canonical document ID.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a SQLite database containing duplicate document records IDs 1, 10, and 11 linked to extracted rows, When scripts/merge_duplicate_documents.py runs in apply mode, Then all child references are re-pointed to the canonical document ID, content_sha256 is backfilled, and redundant duplicate rows are merged without losing any linked records.
Given the migration script is run in dry-run mode or executed a second time, When inspecting the database, Then dry-run makes zero mutations and repeated runs are idempotent with zero errors.
Given a pre-merge backup snapshot, When verifying post-migration integrity, Then total extracted structured record counts before and after merge match 100%.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Foreign-key and document_id reference scatter across structured SQLite tables for legacy IDs 1, 10, and 11
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 orphaned child rows and 100% row-count parity for linked structured records across merge execution

epics.title: Interactive CRUD & Chat-Driven Correction of Extracted Academic DB Records
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator or department head reviews documents uploaded to the CRIE portal, I want CRUD endpoints, conversational agent tools, and structured UI record cards for enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula with SQLite revision logging, so that misparsed fields can be inspected and corrected in place and immediately reflected in subsequent assistant answers.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% persistence fidelity and revision-log traceability for structured edits across enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula reflected in the next conversational turn
epics.tocConstraintRef: Absence of write-back CRUD endpoints, persistent memory tools, and revision auditing linking extracted SQLite tables to chat and UI workflows
requirements: R1: Implement crie_persistent_memory.py with transactional CRUD operations and a SQLite record_revisions audit table capturing timestamp, actor/session, table name, record ID, source document ID, previous value, and updated value for enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula.

R2: Expose REST CRUD endpoints in crie_assistant_api.py to list structured DB records by document ID (covering registry IDs 1-11+), inspect single rows, create/update/delete validated fields (such as trainee full name, specialty, study/funding basis, faculty assignment, or RUP hours), and require explicit confirmation for destructive actions.

R3: Add agent tools in crie_autonomous_agent.py and crie_persistent_memory.py so file uploads or chat queries display a structured card of extracted DB records and execute conversational correction commands directly in SQLite with revision logging.
R4: Guarantee cross-turn SQLite freshness so any field corrected via chat or CRUD API is queried fresh and used accurately in the assistant's very next response.

R5: Build an interactive browser UI record card and inline edit/confirmation dialog in the portal/chat view that preserves user input on validation or connection failures, provides immediate success/error feedback, works on mobile and desktop viewports, and satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA.

R6: Provide realistic CRIE fixture records for document IDs 1-11 across contingent, faculty, and RUP tables and validate the full flow—selecting or uploading a document, issuing a chat correction for an enrolled trainee, confirming the SQLite table update, and verifying the next agent answer—across unit, integration, and E2E tests.

slices.title: Persistent Memory DAL & Revision Audit Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing structured persistence for this epic, I want crie_persistent_memory.py to provide validated SQLite CRUD methods and revision audit logging for enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula, so that all extracted record mutations are atomic and traceable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula, and record_revisions tables in SQLite, When crie_persistent_memory.py updates or deletes a row linked to a document ID, Then the mutation and corresponding revision entry (old value, new value, actor/session, timestamp) commit atomically in one transaction.
Given invalid specialty codes, negative RUP hours, or missing required fields, When validation runs prior to commit, Then the transaction is rejected with a structured validation error and zero partial writes.
Given realistic seeded fixtures for document IDs 1-11, When querying records by document ID, Then matching rows across all three domain tables are returned accurately.
slices.tocConstraintRef: No unified transactional persistence layer or audit trail backing structured DB edits across the three CRIE tables
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% atomic commit-and-audit pairing rate and 0 unlogged mutations on enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula

epics.title: Interactive Record Correction & Cross-Turn Consistency Telemetry (GQM)
epics.jtbd: When operating the CRIE document-to-SQLite record correction workflow, I want Goal-Question-Metric telemetry tracking Goal: enabling administrators to review and correct extracted enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula records without manual database intervention by answering Q1 (do uploaded or selected documents surface complete extracted-record cards?), Q2 (do conversational and CRUD corrections persist with revision logs and propagate accurately into the next assistant turn?), and Q3 (how often do correction attempts fail validation or leave stale agent state?), so that product effectiveness is objectively verified.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 99.5% telemetry capture accuracy for Q1/Q2/Q3 correction workflow outcomes with <0.5% failed or stale-read correction rate
epics.tocConstraintRef: Lack of GQM outcome observability verifying whether interactive record corrections replace manual SQL editing without silent state drift
requirements: R1: Goal & Q1 (Extracted Card Completeness) — Track the percentage of uploaded or inspected documents (IDs 1-11+) whose returned card presents schema-valid DB row counts for enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula.

R2: Q2 (Correction Persistence & Next-Turn Propagation) — Track the percentage of chat and CRUD correction commands that commit a revision-logged SQLite update and match the updated value in the immediately following assistant response.
R3: Q3 (Correction Failure & Stale-State Rate) — Track the rate and categorized cause of failed corrections (validation errors, unresolved record IDs, or stale-context mismatches).
R4: Persist only the GQM metrics answering Q1-Q3 and expose a concise summary endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py without adding unrelated analytics counters.

epics.title: Jargon-Free Live DB Registry Status & File Upload/Correction Guidance
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator or faculty user asks the CRIE assistant how to upload, edit, or use files for data correction, I want all internal prompt-engineering terminology removed from consultant and agent prompts and responses dynamically built from real SQLite document inventories and extracted table counts alongside clear UI instructions, so that users never see confusing internal jargon and always receive accurate backend status.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0 occurrences of prohibited prompt-engineering terms (such as 'slot' or 'system prompt') in chat replies and 100% parity between reported document/row counts and live SQLite state
epics.tocConstraintRef: Hardcoded prompt-engineering terminology in crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py disconnected from live SQLite registry queries
requirements: R1: Purge all internal prompt-engineering jargon (including 'slot to current turn', 'system prompt', and Russian equivalents such as 'слот к текущей реплике' and 'системный промпт') from crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and system prompts in crie_autonomous_agent.py, backed by a deterministic post-generation output sanitizer/guard.

R2: Query live SQLite backend state to retrieve concrete uploaded document names/IDs (e.g., active residency and postgraduate admission orders) and exact extracted record counts across contingent (enrolled_trainees), faculty (pps_staff), and curriculum (rup_curricula) tables.

R3: When users ask about uploading, editing, or using files (including queries on how to send files for data correction), generate a clear response containing (a) the live SQLite document inventory and per-table extracted counts, and (b) a step-by-step UI guide (attach file button -> automatic parsing into DB tables -> review and correct fields directly in chat or table), with graceful messaging when no documents are uploaded yet.
R4: Verify across unit and chat-API integration tests that file-guidance queries contain zero prohibited prompt-slot jargon while displaying real SQLite document statistics and editing instructions.
